Task: make entire-brain's human (TUI) output match the entire CLI's look — adopt the
CLI's palette as brain's default theme and audit every command's output for idiom
parity. This is a stable-release (v0.2.0) gate item.

Context:
- All human output already flows through internal/tui (render.go, tui.go, styles.go;
  charmbracelet lipgloss/bubbletea stack). This is a styling pass, not a refactor.
- styles.go defines a Theme struct and a themes map ("default", "catppuccin", ...),
  selected via --theme / ENTIRE_BRAIN_THEME. The current default is a neutral
  256-color scheme chosen to survive any terminal.
- Decision already made: the default theme should be the entire CLI's palette.

Work:
1. Find the entire CLI's canonical palette in its source (the host `entire` binary's
   repo). If you cannot locate that repo locally, STOP and ask evis for its path —
   do not reconstruct colors by eyeballing screenshots.
2. Add the CLI palette as brain's new default theme. Keep the current default
   available under a name like "neutral" so existing ENTIRE_BRAIN_THEME/--theme
   values keep working (compat policy for this release: no silent breakage — old
   theme names stay valid). If the CLI palette uses truecolor hexes, confirm
   lipgloss/colorprofile downsampling keeps 256-color terminals readable.
3. In styles.go, add a comment naming the file/commit in the entire CLI repo the
   palette was copied from, so the next drift is traceable.
4. Sweep for render-layer bypasses: grep internal/cli (non-test) for fmt.Print*,
   fmt.Fprint*(os.Stdout/os.Stderr) and route survivors through internal/tui.
   A first narrow grep found ~1; use a broader pattern.
5. Build a command census harness: enumerate every command from the help tree and
   run each one (human mode, in a small set-up scratch repo) capturing output to
   files, so a human can page through before/after side by side. Evis will do the
   per-command eyeball pass in this workspace — your job is to make that pass easy
   (one script, one output dir, stable ordering).
6. Fix the obvious idiom drift you see while capturing: error/warning prefix
   style, heading/accent usage, spinner vs progress-bar conventions, table style —
   matched against the entire CLI's conventions, not your taste.

Out of scope, note in the PR: entire-graph needs the same palette adoption in its
own repo; JSON output is untouched (byte-stable JSON is a compat surface).

Verify: `go test ./internal/tui ./internal/cli` plus the capture script run clean.
Normal PR flow: pull latest main, branch, explicit git add of named files, run the
local oxfmt check before push.

92	// ThemeByName resolves a theme by name (case-insensitive), falling back to the
93	// default scheme for an empty or unknown name. The bool reports whether the name
94	// matched a known theme.

96		if t, ok := themes[normalizeThemeName(name)]; ok {
97			return t, true

102	// ThemeNames lists the available theme names (for help text / flag docs),
103	// derived from the themes map so it can never drift out of sync with it. The
104	// default scheme is listed first (it is the fallback); the rest are sorted.
105	func ThemeNames() []string {
106		rest := make([]string, 0, len(themes))
107		for name := range themes {
108			if name != "default" {

116	func normalizeThemeName(name string) string {
117		out := make([]rune, 0, len(name))

121				out = append(out, r+('a'-'A'))

entire-brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI.

It builds a local, inspectable repository brain from retained sessions, seed
context, docs, history, semantic records, and durable memories, then exposes
retrieval, verification, evaluation, and MCP surfaces for agents.

Usage:
  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

Set up the brain & agents:
  setup               Build the brain and start background updates
  add                 Clone a repository, fetch its Entire history, and build its brain
  agent-guide         Preview repository-specific agent instructions
  mcp                 Serve local brain tools over MCP (stdio by default, or HTTP with --http)
  webhook             Notify another service when this brain changes
  config              Inspect or initialize plugin configuration

Search & explore the brain:
  overview            Summarize the project, its structure, and decisions
  brief               Gather relevant context for a task
  query               Search the brain (hybrid by default)
  get                 Fetch a brain item by ID
  multi-get           Fetch multiple brain items by ID
  dash                Browse the brain in an interactive dashboard

Durable memories & patterns:
  recall              Retrieve durable memories matching a query for the current branch
  remember            Record a durable memory about this repository
  distill             Extract durable memories from sessions (requires an agent)
  memories            Review, promote, and garbage-collect durable memories
  connect             Bind this repository to its hosted brain explicitly
  disconnect          Stop syncing this repository with its hosted brain
  verify              Verify durable memory anchors against local retained sources
  patterns            Inspect and rebuild recurring patterns from sessions

Code & semantic index:
  inspect             Explore code, dependencies, and change history
  show                Show one semantic brain record
  viz                 Explore the brain as a graph in your browser

Brain state & maintenance:
  status              Show brain coverage, freshness, and workspace state
  stats               Show brain record counts and breakdowns

Workspaces & sharing:
  workspace           Manage local multi-repo brain workspaces
  bundle              Import or export local brain bundles
  publish             Publish the local brain to hosted Entire (opt-in)

Troubleshooting & operations:
  memories import     Import durable memories from another memory tool's export
  memories sync       Read-merge-CAS this branch's local memories into the shared memory-set head
  memories proposals  Review the hosted cross-member conflict queue (opt-in)
  memories gc         Prune retracted and old superseded memories; report orphans
  memories vitality   Show serve receipts per memory (which memories the read surfaces actually emitted)
  memory              Manage conversation indexing and background jobs
  privacy             Control which captured sessions the brain retains
  entities            Find checkpoints and sessions that changed a symbol
  repair              Rebuild Graph's committed-tree code index
